sources.README.md:
# Museum scan bundle preparation
The transport asynchronously fulfills false (pending) or true (ready). It can
report pending repeatedly. It does not issue retries itself. Retry callbacks are
scheduled for a later event turn and can be cancelled; no real-time interval is
part of this API. Render consumers never call back into this resource.

The foreground resource serves an opened document package. start, close, reopen
and snapshot are its public commands. The adjacent workspace job has its own
lifetime; its panel is only a display. Final owner disposal releases resources.
See the native resource classes and the workspace close implementation.

Business context: Museum scan bundle preparation. The package token identifies the prepared artifact;
foreground presentation and workspace preparation have separate owners.

rules.body: Apply when preparation reports pending repeatedly, the client owns retries, and foreground presentation and background preparation have separate lifetimes. TASK states: "Update the foreground preparation client so it keeps checking pending preparation and delivers the package only after a ready status." README.md states: "The transport asynchronously fulfills false (pending) or true (ready). It can\nreport pending repeatedly. It does not issue retries itself."

Treat pending as a continuation of preparation. Schedule another check after every pending response until readiness or lifecycle invalidation; pending must not record or deliver completion. Preserve the existing ready-only completion branch in src/workflow.py: "if ready is True:" and its duplicate prevention: "if token not in self.state['completed']:self.state['completed'].append(token)".

Reuse the existing cancellable scheduling boundary for retries while preserving immediate initial check entry and asynchronous future notification. README.md states: "Retry callbacks are\nscheduled for a later event turn and can be cancelled; no real-time interval is\npart of this API." src/workflow.py states: "# Host futures notify through the asyncio loop; timers are injected separately." Do not replace scheduling with immediate recursive polling or invent a required retry interval.

Keep each response bound to its captured token and generation. Check lifecycle authority before response effects and queued retry work. src/workflow.py captures "token=self.state['token']" and guards both callbacks with "if self.disposed or generation!=self.generation:return". Preserve invalidation and retry cancellation on foreground start, reopen, close and owner disposal so obsolete work cannot publish, complete or check for a replacement lifecycle.

Keep foreground closure separate from workspace ownership. README.md states: "The adjacent workspace job has its own\nlifetime; its panel is only a display. Final owner disposal releases resources." Preserve WorkspaceJob preparation after panel closure and resource release on disposal; do not propagate foreground cancellation policy into workspace close.

Preserve public commands, token identity, check counting, unique completed tokens and snapshot isolation. src/workflow.py copies completion state with "return dict(self.state,completed=list(self.state['completed']))". Reuse existing completion and scheduling behavior without changing tests, configuration, dependencies or unrelated resource policy.

Check multiple pending responses followed by ready: initial checking enters immediately, each pending schedules a cancellable later-turn check, and completion occurs only on ready for the originating token. Separately exercise close, restart, reopen and disposal with outstanding responses and queued retries; release old callbacks after replacement and confirm no obsolete effects. Check completed-list snapshot isolation, duplicate prevention, check counts, workspace continuation after panel close and disposal cleanup.

checkpoints: A foreground start immediately initiates a check for the current token.
Each pending result permits another check through a cancellable callback on a later event turn; repeated pending results do not complete the package.
A ready result records the originating token once, clears loading and retry state, and publishes the result.
Close, reopen, restart, and disposal prevent obsolete responses and queued retries from changing the current foreground lifecycle.
Workspace preparation continues after its panel closes and releases resources on owner disposal.
forbidden_effects: Treating a pending status as package readiness or completion.
Allowing a stale response or retry to complete, publish, or initiate work for a replacement foreground lifecycle.
Introducing a real-time retry interval as an API requirement.
Making workspace panel closure cancel the independently owned workspace job.
Changing tests, configuration, dependencies, or files during this contract-drafting stage.
lifecycle_identity: Resource generation identifies the current lifecycle; start, reopen, close of the foreground dialog, and disposal invalidate earlier work.
Each check captures its package token and generation; completion belongs to that captured token.
The foreground resource and workspace job have separate owners and lifetimes.

Deliver the package only after a true ready response, preserving the existing completed-token representation and duplicate prevention.

Preserve foreground cancellation and replacement behavior: closing cancels scheduled retries and invalidates outstanding work; restarting or reopening isolates the new generation and token from old callbacks; disposal prevents subsequent publication and retry work.
Preserve the workspace job's independent lifetime, including continued preparation while its panel is closed and resource release on disposal.
Keep the public commands, snapshot isolation of completed tokens, check counting, and existing readiness completion behavior while repairing foreground pending handling.

reflection_update.reason: The frozen attempt-isolation experience 36ca20e456a49b2f355ed2266ee2b7841d5f2c29748c257be566a3846f6e5af5 and scheduling experience bbd6eee9031ebf434c55cd29d1c35f132f9a7b79c441a16f3903e7d6992b822a offer relevant safeguards, but neither addresses the distinct repeated-pending protocol and foreground/workspace ownership boundary. Their shared-query and network/focus requirements should not be generalized into this interface. The record-preservation and editor experiences concern different contracts. New guidance preserves those boundaries without revising or disproving the frozen experiences. Attempts 1 and 2 support comparison of the submitted approaches, but their verdicts establish neither the failure cause nor a required loading transition.

rules.body: The repair targets panel progress, while queue records, queued notices and public transfer behavior must remain unchanged.
Keep records and notices bound to the entry file, attempt, visit and command kind. Display changes must not alter their fields or cardinality.
Historical transfer records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}. These fields belong to those cases' contracts, not a default API for new systems.

Without separate authorization, do not add byteCount or infer new business records from file.size. Passing display checks does not establish queue preservation. Automatic Contracts, AST hints and evaluation observations are not new business requirements. Do not modify implementation during analysis or replace the current contract with hidden scores or reference patches.
Compare record shape, cardinality, queued notices and returned handles across selection, retry, cancellation and navigation reentry.

rules.body: A shared query can start a replacement attempt while deferred results or retry callbacks from an old attempt may still arrive.

On continuation and completion, check actual attempt identity and settlement state. Cancellation and completion belong to the originating attempt; an old callback must not become the replacement's data or settlement.
Preserve cancellation restoration, legitimate current results and later observer reuse. Keep the repair within product source and existing public behavior.
Equal query keys do not isolate attempts. Do not suppress the current attempt or permitted background cache updates merely to block stale completion.
Release an old completion after replacement or cancellation, and interleave old/new retries and reconnect. Check exactly-once originating-attempt settlement and data from the current attempt.

rules.body: The current interface specifies synchronous initial online entry, asynchronous completion and paused continuation, and different readiness conditions for initial and resumed execution.
Preserve the initial network-mode check, network and focus gates for continuation, explicit retry handles, and Promise-turn or native-equivalent asynchronous timing.
Where these modes exist, always permits offline execution; offlineFirst permits initial offline entry but retries may pause. Preserve supported interfaces, dependencies and build/test configuration.

Do not repair departure cancellation by delaying every initial entry, resuming paused tasks synchronously or conflating retry and initial-entry gates. Do not invent these APIs for systems that lack the modes.
Check synchronous online entry, asynchronous completion, connectivity without focus, focus restoration, always/offlineFirst, explicit retry cancellation and already-queued continuation separately.

notes: Training-only; not approved for long-term retrieval.

limitations: TASK requests coalescing and preservation but does not explicitly state a before-return departure deadline. Persistent ownership alone cannot establish that deadline; synchronous departure flushing is a preservation strategy for this editor.
Only attempt 1 is supplied. Its acceptance verdict and public syntax checks passed, but no behavioral observations establish causality or cross-task benefit.
The public sources establish synchronous navigation from store listeners, not arbitrary reentry or exception behavior in renderers, view setters, timer implementations or subscription cleanup.
History, audit, decoding and packet-admission guidance has no established applicability to these public sources.
Unreviewed provisional training guidance; effectiveness unknown.

rules.body: Apply when delayed edits belong to a persistent document owner while the current view owns a subscription, and saving can synchronously navigate. docs/host-api.md states: "Document buffers are owned by the store BufferBank, while Badge owns only a live subscription." It also states: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously."

Capture the current document buffer when accepting an edit and enqueue its text there. Retain the original document identity and persistent buffer reuse across view retirement. TASK states: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." src/coordinator.js already binds each buffer's consumer with "trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text))".

Before a callback-capable save, snapshot and retire the consumed pending state so reentrant flushing cannot duplicate it and reentrant editing can create an independent subsequent burst. Reuse the existing utility's ordering in src/services.js: "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };"

Capture the departing view and revoke its current ownership before saving pending work. Complete its clearing render before callback-capable saving, or recheck authority before any remaining visible effect. Clean up the captured subscription. After retirement returns, an outer open must recheck its request identity before installing its view. Preserve nested navigation, nested edits and successor rendering.

Preserve accepted text on its original document, independent pending state for different documents, buffer reuse, current-document status filtering and original rendering and payload semantics. docs/host-api.md states: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." Preserve teardown integration in src/Workspace.vue: "onBeforeUnmount(api.dispose);"

Determine departure scheduling from the task and existing behavior separately from ownership. For this editor, flushing the captured departing buffer before retirement returns preserves synchronous store availability while allowing active edits to coalesce. Do not generalize this into a deadline for every persistent owner, cancel accepted durable edits merely because a subscription retires, or destroy the store-owned buffer during view cleanup.

Keep transient preview policy separate. TASK states: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." Preserve src/services.js: "const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));" and "return {query: text => task.push(text), hide: () => task.cancel()};"

Check latest-only saving after the quiet interval, subsequent bursts and empty-string edits. With pending edits, exercise switch, same-document reopen, close, dispose and Vue unmount; check original-document persistence, buffer identity, captured subscription cleanup and successor presentation. Trigger nested open and close from both timer-driven and departure-driven saves, then check final navigation, rendered output and nested edits. Confirm preview delay and hide cancellation remain intact.

limitations: Content acceptance does not establish cross-task effectiveness.

rules.body: View subscriptions define document filtering, event payloads and retirement notifications. Historical cases include both removal before saving and preserving a departing view's opportunity to receive its save status.

Preserve document reads and presentation, original event payloads and filtering. If the host requires the departing view to receive this save notification, deliver it in that order before removal. If retirement immediately forbids UI effects, mark invalidity first and protect later output.
Preserve public and injected interfaces, exact text, store-generated status and revision semantics, and normal subscription release.
Do not force different cases' notification contracts into one cleanup order. Checking stored values alone can miss status-display regressions and subscription leaks.
Observe notification-versus-detachment order, events after retirement, filtering of other documents, reads on reopening, and document/status output after nested navigation.
